gaps.sentence: The demonstrators were ___ from entering the building.
gaps.explanation: 'prevent somebody FROM doing' — passive: were prevented from entering.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ told him the truth at the time.
gaps.explanation: 'wish + past perfect' for regret about the past.

gaps.sentence: I'll have finished the report ___ Friday.
The new law comes ___ force next month.
gaps.explanation: 'come into force' = officially start to apply.

gaps.sentence: He must ___ left already — his coat isn't here.
gaps.explanation: 'must have + participle' = certain about the past.

gaps.sentence: The cat cleans ___ after every meal.
gaps.explanation: Reflexive: the cat cleans ITSELF (the object is the same as the subject).

gaps.sentence: She's very good ___ explaining difficult ideas.
The scheme, ___ was announced yesterday, will cost the city millions.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about things take 'which'; 'that' is impossible after a comma.
